# Troubleshooting {#sec-troubleshooting}

Problems seen while building and teaching the workshop, with fixes that were tested. For setup on Windows,
see also [the Windows stuck table](a-windows.qmd#sec-windows-stuck). For anything not listed: copy the command and the whole error into a web chat
with your system's name, try one suggested fix at a time, and never paste passwords or keys.

## Setup {.unnumbered}

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| Mac: a pop-up asks to install "command line developer tools" | Expected the first time `git` runs. Click Install and wait (or run `xcode-select --install` first); if the assistant is waiting, tell it `done` |
| `command not found` for `uv`, `claude`, `codex` or `agy` just after installing | Open a new terminal tab. On a Mac, Claude Code's installer prints a line to add under "Setup notes": paste it, then open the tab |
| `quarto: command not found` in Ubuntu, though it works in PowerShell | Windows installers put tools where Ubuntu cannot use them: install Quarto inside Ubuntu (@sec-step-tools) |
| The prompt shows `/mnt/c/...` | You are in a Windows folder: `cd ~`, and keep projects there |
| `gh auth login` or the assistant cannot open a browser | Expected in WSL: copy the link or code it prints into your Windows browser (for `gh`: github.com/login/device). Codex: `codex login --device-auth` |
| Downloads or `git clone` fail on a company network | A proxy can block `curl`, `git` and `uv`: try another network |
| `git commit` says "Please tell me who you are" | Set your name and email with the two `git config --global` lines from the setup check |
| `not a valid Python environment` | A stale `.venv`: delete it (`rm -rf .venv`); `uv run` rebuilds it |

: Setup problems. {#tbl-trouble-setup}

## Rendering and preview {.unnumbered}

| Problem | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| `readfile 'london.quarto_ipynb'`, or a locked file | A render ran while `quarto preview` was rendering the same file. Let the preview render, or stop it (Ctrl+C) before rendering several formats, then restart it (@sec-render-mechanics) |
| Typst PDF fails: `cannot parse length '60px'` | Typst does not accept CSS pixels in image sizes: write `{height=60}` or `{width="30%"}` |
| A Plotly chart appears twice in a dashboard card | The cell both calls `fig.show()` (or a bare `fig.add_…()`) and returns the figure: assign, and end the cell with `fig` |
| `itables` drops rows from a dashboard table | Its default size limit: `show(df, maxBytes=0)` |
| A Plotly map is a grey rectangle | The GeoJSON's rings wind the other way from Plotly's expectation: reverse them (`load_geojson()` in the water project's script) |
| A page shows old numbers after the data changed | `freeze: auto` reuses results until the page's own source changes: delete `_freeze/` and render again (@sec-water-website) |

: Rendering problems. {#tbl-trouble-render}

## Python and Jupyter {.unnumbered}

| Message | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `quarto check` says Jupyter is not available | Harmless during setup: each project gets its own environment from uv, and Quarto runs Python through `uv run` |
| `Kernel is running over TCP without encryption`, after `[IPKernelApp] WARNING` | Harmless: the connection is between Quarto and a Python process on your own computer |
| `There is an unactivated Python environment in .venv` | Run Quarto through `uv run`, which activates the project's environment |
| A water checkpoint has no data | Water checkpoints hold sources only: `cp -R ../quarto-workshop/examples/water/data .` |

: Python and Jupyter messages. {#tbl-trouble-python}

Backups that copy `.venv/` are slow and pointless, because `uv run` rebuilds it. The checkpoints' backup
command leaves it out, and works on macOS, Linux and WSL:

```bash
b="../project-backup-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)" && mkdir "$b" && tar -cf - --exclude=.venv . | tar -xf - -C "$b"
```

## Publishing {.unnumbered}

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| The first publish fails: "the remote origin does not have a branch named gh-pages" | The first `quarto publish gh-pages` must be interactive: run `uv run quarto publish gh-pages` and press Enter at the question. `--no-prompt` works once the branch exists |
| A push fails with `HTTP 400`, "RPC failed" | `git config http.postBuffer 524288000`, then push again |
| 404 right after publishing | GitHub Pages takes 20 to 60 seconds to deploy: wait a minute and reload (Cmd+Shift+R on a Mac, Ctrl+F5 elsewhere) |
| A link checker reports `403 Forbidden` for a museum's site | Some sites block automated requests: open the link in a browser |

: Publishing problems. {#tbl-trouble-publish}
